spec.name: Rawa Flats — Brutalist Housing Block
spec.description: A raw-concrete brutalist apartment slab on pilotis over a plaza, with stacked window grids, cantilevered front balconies and a taller stair core rising past the roof.
spec.layout: A monumental concrete slab tower, front toward +Z. At the ground: a heavy raised plaza slab (y 0 to 0.3) covering the full footprint, with wide steps at the front and the whole first storey held on chunky pilotis columns (six front, six back) so the lobby glows recessed and glassy underneath. The main tower mass runs y 3.0 to 7.0, a deep concrete exoskeleton: four stacked storeys whose front face is a rigid grid of deep-set window openings — each window is a recessed dark glass panel sunk between chunky concrete mullions and spandrel beams, so the facade reads as coffered raw concrete, not paint. Cantilevered balcony slabs project off the front face (+Z) at each storey line, each with a solid concrete upstand divider wall every bay and a thin metal railing on top; the balcony undersides show raw slab soffits with visible slab edges. At the back (-Z) a service/stair core box rises from first-floor level right through the roof and one full storey above it (to y 8.7), clad in darker board-marked concrete with a vertical strip of narrow slit windows, vents and a canopy door; it carries the rooftop gear on the roof deck: water tank on legs, vent stacks, an antenna mast, and a parapet lip around the roof edge. The style shows everywhere: flat raw concrete in three weathering tones (lighter on up-facing and sunlit faces, darker and mossy low down and in shadow), deep geometric shadow gaps between slabs, banded stains under every balcony edge, small parts in their own colours for glass, railings, doors, vents and drainpipes. Nothing is smooth; edges are chunky, openings are deep, the whole thing reads as poured concrete.

parts.builds: The ground level. A heavy plaza slab (x -3.0..3.0, z -2.5..2.5, y 0..0.3) in plazaGround concrete with a lighter concreteLight top border kerb and a shallow ramp of wide steps at the front edge (z about 2.5..2.9, three chunky steps down to y 0). Above it, the pilotis: ten to twelve solid rectangular concrete columns (roughly 0.45 x 0.45 m) from plaza top y 0.3 up to the first-floor soffit at y 3.0, in two rows (front row near z 1.9, back row near z -1.9, plus mid-row at z 0), concreteMid at the bottom with darker stainBand on the lower third where rain ran down. Between the columns sits the recessed lobby: a glassy box (glass panels with a few glassLit lit panes) set back between columns, with two heavy rustDoor entry doors, a whitePaint lobby sign strip above them, a concreteDark ground-floor ceiling soffit slab capping it all at y 2.7..3.0, and a couple of round ceiling lamps. A thin dark drainpipe drops at one front corner column. Lowest points are the plaza slab and steps at y 0.
parts.attaches: Columns land on the plaza slab (its own top, plazaTop); the soffit slab at y 3.0 meets the tower shell exactly at firstFloorLevel; column positions leave the tower footprint x -2.4..2.4 clear.

parts.builds: The main concrete mass, the hero of the model. A slab block x -2.4..2.4, y 3.0..7.0, z -1.8..1.8, built as an exposed concrete exoskeleton rather than a plain box: four stacked storeys, each with a thick front and back band of vertical concrete mullions (about 7 bays across the front) and horizontal spandrel beams at every floor line, so the window openings between them are truly recessed. Each window opening gets a dark glass panel (glass) seated deep inside the reveal, with two or three panes per storey glowing glassLit, plus a thin whitePaint or concreteDark sill. The concrete faces use all four tones: concreteLight on sunlit top edges and upstands, concreteMid on main faces, concreteDark in the deep window reveals and under-beam shadow, stainBand as weathering streaks below window corners. End walls (left x 2.4 and right x -2.4) are mostly blind concrete with a few small punched slit windows in glass and a vertical drainpipe each, concreteDark. The back face (z -1.8) is plainer raw concreteMid with a regular grid of small dark windows. Top of the mass at y 7.0 meets the roofDeck; leave a slot at the back x -1.3..1.3, z -1.8..-0.9 clear where the service core passes through.
parts.attaches: Sits on the pilotis soffit exactly at firstFloorLevel (mount); roof at y 7.0 is the roofDeck mount; back slot is shared with the core at backCoreLine; front face at z 1.8 is where balconies bolt on.

parts.builds: The cantilevered front balconies, the signature silhouette. Four balcony slabs, one per storey, projecting from the front face z 1.8 out to z 2.55, each spanning x -2.3..2.3, about 0.18 m thick, in concreteLight (sun catches the slab tops and fascia edges). Each slab shows its raw underside soffit in concreteDark with a banded stainBand weathering streak running along the outer fascia below every edge. On each balcony: solid concrete upstand divider walls (about 1.0 m high, 0.12 thick, one between each of the ~6 bays, splitting it into apartments) in concreteMid with lighter tops, and on top of the slab edge away from the dividers a thin metalDark railing of simple vertical bars with a rustDoor handrail. A few balcony floors get small details: a moss-green planter box, a whitePaint drying-rack or a dark door frame recessed into the facade glass line. The lowest balcony at y 3.0 overlaps the plaza below, so its edge casts the deep shadow gap the style needs. Nothing touches the floor; everything is carried on the towerShell front face.
parts.attaches: Slabs root into the towerShell front face at z 1.8 at each storey line (y 3.0, 4.0, 5.0, 6.0); outer edges hang free above the plazaAndPilotis steps.

parts.builds: The stair/service core that punches above the roofline. A tall box x -1.3..1.3, z -1.9..-0.9, running from first-floor level y 3.0 up to y 8.7, one full storey above the main roof at 7.0. Clad in the darkest concrete (concreteDark) with board-marked banding (thin horizontal concreteShadow ribs every ~0.5 m) so it reads as a different, harder pour than the tower. Its back and side faces carry a vertical strip of narrow slit windows in glass, one pane lit glassLit near the top. At first-floor level on its side face: a rustDoor service door with a small concreteDark canopy slab over it. Above the main roof it becomes the penthouse housing the lift machine room: a heavier cap slab, two or three large vent louvre openings (ventGrey slats) on each face, a small whitePaint painted sign panel, and a thin parapet upstand. Its very top edge is capped in concreteLight. Protruding stub pipes in metalDark where it meets the roof deck. The core spans continuously from firstFloorLevel through roofDeck to its cap.
parts.attaches: Rises through the towerShell back slot (its walls are the slot walls) resting at firstFloorLevel, passes through the roofDeck plane at y 7.0, and stands free above it.

parts.builds: Everything on the roof deck at y 7.0, kept simpler than the facade. A parapet lip (0.25 m high, 0.15 thick) in concreteMid running around the tower roof edge x -2.4..2.4, z -1.8..1.8, skipping the core slot at the back. Inside: a rooftop water tank on four short legs in the left-front quadrant — a squat cylinder in concreteMid with a concreteDark coned top, a metalDark access ladder and a small vent cap; two or three squat vent stacks (ventGrey cylinders with metalDark caps) scattered on the right side; a slim antenna mast (metalDark rod about 1.6 m with two crossbars and a small glassLit red lamp at the tip) near the back right; a skylight box (glass with whitePaint frame) mid-roof; and patches of moss where the roof membrane has cracked, plus a stainBand drip trail running over the parapet on one side. A short metalDark stair-bulkhead door leans against the core wall. All resting on the roofDeck plane; nothing hangs off the model edge except the antenna tip, well inside the bounding box.
parts.attaches: Everything stands on the towerShell roof plane (roofDeck mount, y 7.0) and clears the serviceCore box; the parapet sits on the tower's outer edge line.

Brutalist housing block: tower of stacked concrete slabs, deep-set windows grid, pilotis, cantilevered balconies, service tower with stairwell core, ground plaza with columns. Style: raw concrete, repeating window grid, weathering.

Let me define the model: A large apartment slab block, maybe 4.5m wide (x), 6m tall (y), 10m deep (z)? "front faces +Z". Brutalist housing block — a big tower. Let's set size [5, 7.5, 4.5] maybe. Or a long slab: width x = 6, height 8, depth z = 3.5. Standing on pilotis? Brutalist blocks often sit on pilotis (corb) or heavy plinth. Let's do: heavy plinth (raised entry level on pilotis/columns), main tower of stacked floors, cantilevered balconies with dividers, top mechanical penthouse / stair core tower, ground plaza.

2. tower body: stacked floors with window grid — repeated concrete frames, window bands. Attaches to plinth top mount.
3. balconies/fins: cantilevered slabs with upstand dividers on front face.
